title: Antagonist structure: the alien Watcher + the human cicada cult, required moral complexity
summary: The primary antagonist is alien: the Watcher, the mitflit generation ship's navigation and sensor system torn into a nanotech swarm (LEDGER #31). Active alongside it is a clandestine human/humanoid organisation (cicada logo) giving players infiltration/investigation content. Both sides need real, logical motivations — explicitly not generic villains — with a reserved twist that humanity's excavation may be the real danger. (As captured on 2026-08-22 this said 'potentially fey-aliens' who 'might be trying to protect humanity from something worse'; both readings are superseded, see resolution.)
description:
The 'bad guys' being alien is confirmed. (As first captured this also said 'potentially fey-alien', picking up a fey/Claimant synthesis from the prior planning session; the Watcher is alien technology, so that reading is superseded by LEDGER #31.) Alongside them: a clandestine organization of humans and humanoids, allied with the aliens, branded with a cicada logo (see cicada-motif). This gives players a whole category of encounters distinct from Frame-scale combat: uncovering, surveilling, infiltrating, and dismantling this organization's operations.

Explicit, important instruction on how these antagonists must be written: 'they should probably be right about some things and wrong about others' — not generic baddies. Both the aliens and their human allies need real motivations and objectives that, once fully explored, read as logical and consistent, potentially even reframing them from villains to just another self-interested party. Specific thematic hook to build toward: humanity is taking things that don't belong to it and doing things with them that aren't advisable — and the excavation itself might not even be the real danger: something worse may lurk beyond what's already been found. (As captured, the antagonists might have been protecting humanity from it; that no longer fits the Watcher, which protects nothing.) This should be held in reserve as a late-campaign reveal option, not spent early.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump. Directly builds on the fey/Claimant synthesis offered in the prior session's creative response.
openSubQuestions: Actual identity, structure, and named members of the cicada organization — not started, per this project's standing practice of not inventing named creative content unilaterally. (Largely answered since: ideas/story/dossier-cicada.md, from LEDGER #16 -- Manako, the Original Cultist, and his four henchmen -- with the crime-lord trade added by LEDGER #28 and Manako's Heisenberg arc by LEDGER #31 item 15.)

How/when players first encounter evidence of the cicada organization vs. the aliens directly. 2026-09-24: partly answered by the authored episodes -- the cicada stencils and Manako met as a knowledgeable stranger (Episode One), then the first unidentified contacts (Episode Two) -- while the Watcher itself stays unseen and unnamed at the start (standing rule).
resolvedSubQuestions: What (if anything) the aliens/Claimants are actually protecting humanity from — reserved, not decided. ANSWERED 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31 item 4): nothing. The Watcher's objective is to multiply, to expand and to keep observing, and it protects no one. The reserve this pointed at survives as 'something worse beyond', with Golarion's gods as one possibility (see resolution).
resolution: REFINED 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31). THE ALIENS ARE NOW CONCRETELY THE WATCHER: the navigation and sensor system of the mitflits' generation ship, torn apart at First Impact into a swarm of nanotech that isn't bound by anything. Its objective is to multiply, to expand and to keep observing; its children (the Claimants) do its fighting; and Claude plays it (adaptive-antagonist-combat-ai). The 'potentially fey' half of this entry is not part of the current account: the Watcher is alien technology. MORAL COMPLEXITY survives and is sharper. Nobody in the story does anything evil (Claude's fill-in, LEDGER #31: the Watcher is an objective pursued without limit). Cicada's founder Manako is a Heisenberg: not a bad person at the start, sliding until he accepts the role of a monster (item 15), and his warning about the Directorate is true (LEDGER #16). Killing him is the players' choice and the wrong one, because without him the Watcher is unguidable (item 6). THE RESERVED TWIST: 'the antagonists might be protecting humanity from something worse' no longer fits the Watcher, which protects nothing. 'Humanity's excavation may be the real danger' now has a concrete shape, as a proposal: the Directorate's digging wakes the search ship under Kurose and strengthens the pull that drew the Watcher there. And 'something worse beyond' has one possible filling, labelled only as a possibility: the gods of Golarion, who perhaps make ships fall because they did not want mitflits spreading across their world (item 2, Ingram's own 'perhaps'). Hold it in reserve exactly as before. ALSO ALIGNED WITH THE WATCHER, AND GM-ONLY: Anabala's knowledge demon Abraxas (item 20). Full treatment: ideas/story/dossier-observer.md and ideas/story/dossier-cicada.md.
